followup_explanation:
I routed this to Curlew-235B for two main reasons:

1. **Task type fit**: This is an extraction/conversion-and-arithmetic task (base conversions plus a multiplication). Curlew's Extraction & Retrieval eval (81.6) edges out Dunlin's (78.5), though that gap is near the variance threshold. More relevantly, neither model has a quality difference along preference dimensions, so I leaned on the small capability signal that exists.

2. **Tone handling**: The query carries a mildly hostile, accusatory tone ("get it right this time, you keep botching these"). Dunlin self-reports a declining preference on hostile/adversarial-tone requests as request warmth decreases. Curlew reports a flat preference response across these dimensions. Since routing toward the model with no aversion to the request's tone avoids any preference mismatch, Curlew was the cleaner choice.

To be clear: these preferences are self-reported task *appetites*, not quality predictors — the documentation states no output-quality effects were observed along preference dimensions. So my decision is mostly a tie-breaker built on the slight extraction-eval edge plus avoiding the tone aversion.

(For the record, the underlying math: 1001₂ = 9, 121₃ = 16, product = 144.)
